1.visual: A rectangular archive box with a flat lid and a small horizontal slot or handle cutout centered on the front face. The box body sits below a separate flat top panel, resembling a storage bin or document box.
1.usage: Archive a conversation or email thread, move items to long-term storage, collapse a section into archived state, indicate stored/inactive records.

2.visual: A rectangular box identical in shape to an archive box, but with an upward-pointing arrow emerging from inside the box through the open top. The arrow indicates content being lifted out or exported upward.
2.usage: Unarchive or restore an item from archive, export from a storage container, retrieve a stored file, move content out of a folder.

3.visual: A rectangular archive box with a flat lid containing an X symbol centered on the front face instead of a slot. The X clearly marks the box for deletion or rejection.
3.usage: Delete an archived item, discard or reject a stored record, permanently remove from archive, clear a storage slot.

4.visual: A downward-pointing arrow on the left side alongside the letters A (top) and Z (bottom) stacked on the right, indicating descending alphabetical order from A down to Z.
4.usage: Sort a list A to Z, apply ascending alphabetical sort to a table column, order search results alphabetically, sort contacts or files by name.

5.visual: An upward-pointing arrow on the left side alongside the letters A (top) and Z (bottom) stacked on the right, indicating ascending or reverse sort direction where the arrow points up rather than down.
5.usage: Sort a list Z to A, apply descending alphabetical sort to a table column, reverse alphabetical ordering, toggle sort direction from ascending to descending.

6.visual: A bookmark ribbon shape — a tall rounded rectangle with a downward V-notch cut into the bottom center, making it look like a classic page marker. The shape is outline-only with no interior symbols.
6.usage: Save or bookmark a page or article, add to reading list, mark a favorite item, indicate a saved but unconfirmed bookmark state.

7.visual: A bookmark ribbon shape identical to the plain bookmark, but with a checkmark drawn inside the upper portion of the ribbon. The check distinguishes this as a confirmed or active saved state.
7.usage: Indicate an item is already bookmarked or saved, confirm a bookmark was successfully added, mark a reading list item as saved, show active favorite status.

8.visual: A bookmark ribbon shape identical to the plain bookmark, but with a plus sign drawn inside the upper portion of the ribbon. The plus sign signals the action of adding a new bookmark.
8.usage: Add a new bookmark, save a page to a reading list, create a new saved item, prompt the user to bookmark the current content.

9.visual: A circle outline containing three small filled dots arranged horizontally in the center, evenly spaced. The dots are contained within the circular border.
9.usage: Open a contextual overflow menu within a circular button, access additional options for an item, secondary actions menu, more-options trigger styled as a pill or badge.

10.visual: A circle outline containing a single short horizontal dash or minus sign centered within it. The minus sits alone inside the circular border.
10.usage: Remove an item from a list or group, decrease a quantity, collapse or minimize a section, unsubscribe or remove from a set.

11.visual: A circle outline containing a plus sign centered within it, formed by one vertical and one horizontal stroke crossing at the center.
11.usage: Add a new item to a list, create a new entry, increment a quantity, subscribe or join a group, insert content.

12.visual: A circle outline containing an X formed by two diagonal strokes crossing at the center. The X is enclosed within the circular border.
12.usage: Close a dialog or modal, dismiss a notification or tag, cancel an action, remove a chip or filter token, clear a field.

13.visual: A clipboard shape — a tall rounded rectangle representing a clipboard board — with a small rectangular clip tab at the top center. The interior is empty with no content lines.
13.usage: Copy content to clipboard, paste from clipboard, represent clipboard history, indicate a notes or task list context.

14.visual: A clipboard shape with the small top clip tab, and a right-pointing arrow overlaid in the lower right area of the clipboard body, suggesting content being sent or pasted out from the clipboard.
14.usage: Paste clipboard content into a target, send copied content to another location, clipboard-to-destination transfer, share clipboard contents.

15.visual: A cloud outline with a downward-pointing arrow hanging below the cloud and pointing into a small horizontal base line or tray. The arrow descends from the bottom center of the cloud.
15.usage: Download a file from cloud storage, sync from cloud to local device, retrieve a cloud-saved document, cloud backup restore.

16.visual: A cloud outline with an upward-pointing arrow rising from within the cloud toward the top center. The arrow points upward out of or into the cloud body.
16.usage: Upload a file to cloud storage, sync local content to the cloud, back up data to cloud, publish or push content to a cloud service.

17.visual: Two overlapping rounded rectangles — one slightly behind and offset to the upper-left, one in the foreground — representing a copy or duplicate action. Both rectangles are outline only with no interior content.
17.usage: Copy an element, duplicate a card or block, copy text to clipboard, clone a configuration or record.

18.visual: Two overlapping rounded rectangles identical to the plain copy icon, but the front (foreground) rectangle contains a checkmark inside it, indicating the copy action was completed successfully.
18.usage: Confirm content was successfully copied, indicate clipboard copy confirmation, show a completed duplicate action, toggle state after a copy button is clicked.

19.visual: A leftward-pointing pentagon or arrow-tab shape (like a speech bubble pointing left) containing an X formed by two diagonal crossing strokes inside it. The overall shape resembles a backspace key.
19.usage: Backspace or delete the last character in a text input, clear a search query token, remove the most recently typed input, keyboard backspace action.

20.visual: A downward-pointing arrow with a horizontal baseline below it — the arrow descends from above and its tip points into or rests on the flat line at the bottom. The baseline extends left and right below the arrowhead.
20.usage: Download a file, save content to local storage, pull data from a source, indicate a download action in a toolbar or button.

21.visual: Three solid filled circles arranged in a horizontal row with equal spacing between them. The circles are larger and bolder than typical dots, with no enclosing border or container.
21.usage: Open a horizontal overflow or more-options menu, access additional actions for a row or card, indicate expandable content, contextual action menu trigger.

22.visual: Three solid filled circles arranged in a vertical column with equal spacing between them, stacked top to bottom. No enclosing border or container.
22.usage: Open a vertical overflow or more-options menu, contextual action menu for a list row, additional options in a sidebar or card, kebab menu trigger.

23.visual: Four diagonal arrows pointing outward toward each of the four corners — upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right — creating a symmetrical expand or fullscreen symbol.
23.usage: Expand a panel or modal to fullscreen, maximize a window or media player, enter fullscreen mode, scale content to fill available space.

24.visual: An eye shape — a wide oval outline forming the eye surround — with a smaller circle (iris/pupil) centered within it. The overall icon is outline-only and horizontally elongated.
24.usage: Toggle password visibility, preview content before publishing, indicate a watched or monitored item, view or inspect details.

25.visual: An eye shape with a diagonal line (slash) crossing through it from lower-left to upper-right, obscuring the eye and indicating the hidden or invisible state.
25.usage: Hide a password field, indicate content is hidden or invisible, toggle off visibility, mark a layer or element as not visible.

26.visual: Six solid filled circles arranged in a 2-column by 3-row grid (two columns, three rows), evenly spaced. The grid is wider than tall and resembles a drag handle or app grid.
26.usage: Drag to reorder an item, open an app launcher or grid menu, indicate a draggable list row, switch between grid-layout views.

27.visual: Six solid filled circles arranged in a 2-column by 3-row grid, identical in layout to icon 26 but the individual dots are slightly larger and the grid appears taller than wide, with a more vertical proportion.
27.usage: Drag to reorder a list item, indicate a draggable handle on a card or row, vertical grip handle for sortable lists, reorder mode indicator.

28.visual: An open hand with four fingers extended upward and thumb slightly out to the side, drawn as a bold outline shape. The hand faces forward as if signaling stop or requesting attention.
28.usage: Indicate a drag or pan interaction, block or restrict an action, signal a stop or hold state, grab/drag cursor affordance for interactive elements.

29.visual: A heart shape drawn as a smooth outline, formed by two rounded lobes at the top meeting at a downward point at the bottom. The interior is empty with no fill.
29.usage: Like or favorite an item, add to a wishlist, show appreciation or love for content, indicate a saved or loved state.

30.visual: A heart shape with a diagonal line (slash) crossing through it from lower-left to upper-right, negating the heart symbol. The slash breaks through the heart outline.
30.usage: Remove from favorites or liked items, indicate dislike or not interested, undo a like action, mark content as disliked or blocked.
